userStories.title: Derive allowed command candidates from base-commit package scripts
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Implement the deterministic candidate rule, base-manifest reader and readable command/protected-path helpers in workflow/config-change.ts.

**Motivation** — The owner ruled (2026-11-13) that no model decides whether a command is safe: `quality.commands` run through a shell outside the permission gate, so the allowed changes are fixed by a rule nax evaluates, and the advisor only chooses among them.

**Approach** — **The rule.** For a story whose package dir `<pkg>` (its `workdir` relative to the repo root) is not the repo root, with story base commit `<base>` (`sc.base`):

- The gate-to-key map is `GATE_COMMAND_KEY`: `lint` → `lint`, `typecheck` → `typecheck`, `scoped` → `testScoped`, `full-suite` → `test`.
- The red gates are the gates whose state is `"red"` in the story loop's last gate run (`gates.states` only; the full-suite result `suite.states` is not read). With no red gate there are no candidates.
- The candidate values come from the `scripts` object of `<pkg>/package.json` **as committed at `<base>`** (read with `git show <base>:<pkg>/package.json`), in the object's key order. For every script value `v`: the candidate `v`, and for the key `testScoped` only, also `v + " {{files}}"`. A candidate equal to the key's current command is dropped. A quality command is a string or a non-empty string array (`QualityCommandSpecSchema`); an array command is never equal to a candidate, and wherever a command is shown or stored as `from` it is rendered by `renderCommandSpec`: a string as is, an array as its elements joined with ` && `. Duplicates (same key and value) are kept once, the first script in key order wins.
- The base commit is used so a session cannot add a script during this story and then have it offered.
- A story whose package is the repo root gets no candidates: root config is cached for the whole run outside the package registry (`_rootConfigCache` in `config/loader.ts`, and `PackageRegistry.resolve("")` returns `loader.current()`), so a change there could not reach the run's later gates.

The pure function emits candidates grouped in the supplied red-gate order. The story-env caller enforces the non-root eligibility before offering candidates. `readBaseScripts` returns `{}` on a missing/unreadable base manifest, non-zero or throwing git, invalid JSON, or no scripts object, so the advisor can retain answer/hold only. `protectedPathList` is `[policy.projectStateDir + "/", policy.credentialDir + "/", policy.trustStoreFile]`.

**Scope** — In: new module, pure rule, base-commit reader, rendering, policy list, injected git dependency and its unit tests. Out: advisor-menu construction (US-001), tracked-file checks/writes/commits/cache reload (US-003), env wiring (US-004), loop/state/status (US-005/US-006); no working-tree scripts, edited flags or runner-run-script candidates. Feature boundaries: Config keys other than `quality.commands.lint`, `quality.commands.typecheck`, `quality.commands.testScoped` and `quality.commands.test`. Candidate forms other than a base-commit script value and, for `testScoped`, that value plus ` {{files}}`: no `<runner> run <script>` forms and no edited flags.

**Interface** —
```typescript
const GATE_COMMAND_KEY: Readonly<Record<GateName, QualityCommandKey>>;
function configChangeCandidates(input: { redGates: readonly GateName[]; commands: Readonly<Partial<Record<QualityCommandKey, string | readonly string[]>>>; scripts: Readonly<Record<string, string>> }): ConfigChangeCandidate[];
function readBaseScripts(projectDir: string, base: string, packageDir: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>;
function renderCommandSpec(spec: string | readonly string[] | undefined): string | undefined;
function protectedPathList(policy: ProtectedPathsPolicy): string[];
```
`script` is the `package.json` script name the value came from. `renderCommandSpec` returns a string as is, an array joined with ` && `, `undefined` as `undefined`. Create `_configChangeDeps` with git injectable here; US-003 extends it to `{ git, loadConfigForPackage, readFile, writeFile }`. Keep no-facts advisor behavior unchanged if consolidating array rendering into this helper.

userStories.title: Stop unchanged BLOCKED gate loops and show config-change outcomes in status
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Route unchanged BLOCKED gate failures to the existing residual exit early and expose recorded config-change outcomes in plain/JSON workflow status.

**Motivation** — After `BLOCKED`, the loop went on to the next fix round.

**Approach** — **Early stop (#2899).** `evaluateStep` reads the previous pass's red gates from `state.gates` (before the new gate run overwrites it). When `lastTurn.status` is `BLOCKED`, `lastTurn.configApplied` is not true, the previous pass had red gates, and the new pass's red gates are the same set, it sets `advisorRoute`, so `passExit` returns `"capped"` and the story goes to `residualStep` now. The carrier is the existing `lastTurn` key; no new graph state key is added.

Compare only gates.states, not suite.states; compare sets rather than ordering or finding IDs. An applied config change, a changed red set, a DONE reply or no previous in-memory gate pass never triggers this additional early-stop rule. Keep existing cost/no-op/narrower residual rules and terminal residual behavior. Do not hydrate previous-pass gates from resumed records for this feature. Ledger line: `fix round r1 blocked with scoped unchanged: <open ids> go to the advisor`; with lint and scoped the gate text is `lint, scoped`. Name the current open finding IDs.

`nax workflow status` (`packages/nax/src/cli/workflow.ts`): `WorkflowStatusReport` gains optional `configChanges?: readonly ({ storyId: string } & ConfigChangeRecord)[]`, present only when a story recorded one; `printPlain` prints one line per change after the open-item lines. Flatten story record changes without losing round, key, from, to, applied, reason or decisionId. Preserve all existing report fields, live-status overlay behavior, read-only behavior and exit-code semantics. An old record or no recorded changes omits configChanges entirely, not an empty array.

Applied plain line: `US-007 config change applied: quality.commands.testScoped "bun test {{files}}" -> "bun test --isolate {{files}}" (advisor D-3)`. Refused plain line: `US-007 config change refused (untracked): quality.commands.testScoped -> "bun test --isolate {{files}}" (advisor D-3)`. Use each record's story ID and values, not hardcoded example constants.

**Scope** — In: evaluateStep set comparison and advisorRoute/ledger wiring, optional report field/aggregation, plain status lines, blocked-stop unit tests and existing CLI suite extensions. Out: candidate/application/env/absorbTurn implementation (US-001–US-005), graph produces changes, resumed prior-pass reconstruction, run-summary additions and residual config menus. Feature boundaries: The early stop for the first fix round after a resume: a resumed story has no previous pass in memory, so its first pass is compared against nothing. A run-summary line for config changes: they appear in the ledger and in `nax workflow status` only.

**Interface** —
```typescript
// WorkflowStatusReport gains:
configChanges?: readonly ({ storyId: string } & ConfigChangeRecord)[];
// Read existing StoryLoopState.lastTurn.configApplied and WorkflowStoryRecord.configChanges.
// No additional graph state keys or STORY_GRAPH produces entries.
```
Every new record and report field is optional and absent when empty. No migration of prior result.json records or change to schemaVersion is required.

routing.reasoning: A gate-set comparison reuses the existing advisorRoute/capped exit, and optional record flattening extends the existing CLI formatter; these bounded changes introduce no authorization logic or new state-machine abstraction.

When buildReport overlays live forge status, existing recorded configChanges remain in the returned report.

analysis:
Goal and authority: close #2897/#2898/#2899 by supplying advisor facts, offering only deterministic base-manifest command candidates, applying a selected change in the orchestrator, and stopping an unchanged BLOCKED gate loop. This is an enhancement entirely within packages/nax, not a new service or a permission-policy redesign. The binding implementation order is exactly US-001 -> US-002 -> US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005 -> US-006. Codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host; findings below come from direct reads and text search. No source changes or test execution were performed while drafting this PRD. Read docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:13 and the relevant focused conventions before implementation; use Bun, strict TypeScript, injected external dependencies, existing test helpers and package-scoped commands.

Advisor surface and downstream impact: packages/nax/src/advisor/types.ts:9 defines evidence sources, :18 the AdviceAction discriminated union, :38 fixed option parameters, and :120 MenuFacts. packages/nax/src/advisor/menus.ts:9 and :26 are exhaustive label and text-field maps, :45 assigns deterministic option IDs, :157 builds menus, :193 converts a fixed option plus reply text to an action, and :233 forces confirmation for low confidence, irreversible replies or an explicit flag. Keep forcedConfirm unchanged. packages/nax/src/operations/advise.ts:31 deliberately mirrors REQUIRED_TEXT_FIELD so operations imports advisor types rather than advisor runtime values; update both maps without introducing an import cycle. validateAdvisorReply at :63 already rejects off-menu option IDs and empty required fields, so the model must only choose an ID and reason, never construct a key, path or command. packages/nax/src/advisor/index.ts:40 already exports all types. packages/nax/src/advisor/decision-log.ts:13 formats actions through private actionText; exercise the new branch via describeRuling/decisionLine rather than requiring a new public API. packages/nax/src/workflow/advisor.ts:21 currently returns string|null, and packages/nax/src/workflow/advisor-live.ts:77 builds the question with concern evidence first and answer/hold only. Preserve plain-string answers, null/default hold, exception containment and no-facts exact shapes. US-001 widening the return union also affects the caller at packages/nax/src/workflow/story-steps.ts:198; keep intermediate stories type-safe by narrowing strings there, without implementing config application before US-005.

Candidate authority and trust boundary: packages/nax/src/agents/nax-protected-paths.ts:21 supplies projectStateDir, credentialDir and trustStoreFile from the same live policy used by tools; display these facts without modifying policy or sessions. packages/nax/src/config/schemas-execution.ts:263 permits quality commands as strings or non-empty string arrays, with testScoped at :273. Do not equate a rendered array to a string candidate: equality uses the original command spec; rendering is for evidence/from only. Red-gate eligibility must read gates.states exclusively, not the existing merged gates/suite helper. Base scripts come from git show <sc.base>:<pkg>/package.json, never the working tree or current HEAD. All string script values are eligible, independent of their script name; only testScoped receives the additional literal suffix ' {{files}}'. Preserve red-gate order, script object key order and first-wins deduplication by key/value. Missing, malformed or unreadable base manifests fail closed to {}. The candidate module is new in US-002; US-001 must not import a not-yet-created module. There is a local spec type inconsistency: ImplementerQuestionFacts.commands is described as string-only but US-001 AC17 explicitly passes an array command. AC17 is authoritative: allow readonly string[] at the advisor facts boundary and render it with the stipulated join, while buildStoryEnv can supply normalized strings. Implement renderCommandSpec in US-002 and reuse/consolidate the renderer after that dependency exists rather than adding a forward dependency from US-001.

Config/cache architecture: packages/nax/src/config/package-config-cache.ts:30 exposes the existing whole-cache clear; packages/nax/src/config/loader.ts:312 has a separate root promise cache. packages/nax/src/config/package-config.ts:33 requires the current config to inherit the --profile chain and pins root-only keys; always use this helper on reload, not an unprofiled loadConfigForWorkdir call. packages/nax/src/runtime/packages.ts:36 defines PackageRegistry, :65 creates immutable views with selector memoization, :145 creates the registry caches, :173 resolves a view from mergedConfigs or loader.current(), :217 hydrates one override, and :233 skips already-hydrated packages. Add refresh in US-003 to bypass that skip and invalidate cached identity views for the same override, including worktree identities, while preserving unrelated package views and path identity.
